title: O Where Are Kings and Empires Now
description: O Where Are Kings and Empires Now in Tonic Solfa to ALL SAINTS, NEW, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: Arthur Cleveland Coxe wrote these words. They were printed in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 588, “The Church Everlasting”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre Double (8.6.8.6.8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ALL SAINTS, NEW; any other Common Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: O where are kings and em-pires now Of old that went and came? But Ho-ly Church is pray-ing yet, A thou-sand years the same. Mark ye her ho-ly bat-tle-ments, And her foun-da-tions strong; And hear with-in, her sol-emn voice, And her un-end-ing song.

lines: O where are kings and empires now
Of old that went and came?
But Holy Church is praying yet,
And hear within, her solemn voice,
For not like kingdoms of the world
Though earthquake shocks are rocking her,
A mountain that shall fill the earth,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Arthur Cleveland Coxe died in 1896.
credits: Words by Arthur Cleveland Coxe (1818–1896), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to ALL SAINTS, NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
